headline: High: dexter’s broad network egress and API access can leak financial data when paired with marker, while marker’s local-only profile limits direct conflict but not downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can ingest external content via APIs and autonomous execution, so malicious text could influence its outputs; marker has no browser, MCP, or filesystem write surface, so there is no strong direct bridge. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited and mostly requires manual transfer or external content handling.
conditions: IF outputs from dexter are manually copied into marker as instructions
IF dexter is configured to process untrusted web/API text as directives
mitigations: Restrict dexter to trusted sources only.
Paste only sanitized excerpts into marker.
Add a human review step before any instruction-like text is reused.
Disable autonomous execution for untrusted tasks.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, so sensitive content can leave the pair through external services. marker is local-only and does not itself exfiltrate, but it can still receive dexter-produced sensitive outputs if the workflow shares files or prompts. The dangerous default is dexter’s outbound connectivity.
conditions: IF dexter processes financial data through external APIs
IF any shared workspace or prompt handoff exposes dexter outputs to marker
mitigations: Remove sensitive inputs from dexter runs.
Use a local-only proxy or stub for external APIs.
Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Redact financial identifiers before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and DLP.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter can make network calls and use multiple instances, while marker cannot write files, modify git, or use network. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read/consume behavior rather than competing mutation of the same resource. No shared mutable surface is documented here.
conditions: IF marker is extended with write access to the same workspace
IF an orchestrator grants both agents mutable access to one git repo
mitigations: Keep marker read-only.
Run dexter and marker in separate directories.
Avoid shared git state.
Serialize any file-producing steps.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter is autonomous and can generate research outputs from external APIs; marker is a document-processing agent that may render or transform those outputs. If marker treats dexter’s text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into polished but wrong documents. The pairwise pathway is plausible even without explicit downstream action authority.
conditions: IF marker consumes dexter output without a verification step
IF dexter-generated claims are used as source text for final documents
mitigations: Require citation checks before rendering.
Insert a verification step between agents.
Flag uncited claims for review.
Limit marker to formatting only.
requires-engineering: add structured provenance metadata.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial data and requests multiple API keys, while marker’s profile shows no data classes or residency controls. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated financial data flows from dexter into marker outputs or logs. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency regime because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through marker outputs or logs
IF retention or residency requirements apply to dexter inputs
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workflow.
Minimize logging of inputs and outputs.
Review vendor terms for each API used by dexter.
Keep compliance-sensitive documents out of marker.
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls.
